metadata.title: The sphere packing problem in dimension 8

nodes.name: Sphere packing
nodes.statement: Let $X \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a discrete set with $\|x-y\| \geq 2$ for distinct $x,y \in X$. The set $\mathcal{P} = \bigcup_{x \in X} B_d(x,1)$ is a sphere packing; if $X$ is a lattice it is a lattice sphere packing.

nodes.name: Density of a packing
nodes.statement: $\Delta_{\mathcal{P}} := \limsup_{r \to \infty} \Delta_{\mathcal{P}}(r)$ where $\Delta_{\mathcal{P}}(r) := \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{P} \cap B_d(0,r))/\mathrm{Vol}(B_d(0,r))$.

nodes.name: Sphere packing constant
nodes.statement: $\Delta_d := \sup_{\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^d \text{ sphere packing}} \Delta_{\mathcal{P}}$, the supremum of densities over all $d$-dimensional sphere packings.

nodes.name: $E_8$-lattice
nodes.statement: $\Lambda_8 = \{(x_i) \in \mathbb{Z}^8 \cup (\mathbb{Z}+\tfrac12)^8 \mid \sum_{i=1}^8 x_i \equiv 0 \pmod{2}\}$; the unique up to isometry positive-definite, even, unimodular lattice of rank 8.

nodes.name: Fourier transform
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}(f)(y) = \widehat{f}(y) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(x)\, e^{-2\pi i x \cdot y}\, dx$ for $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

nodes.name: Schwartz function
nodes.statement: A $C^\infty$ function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{C}$ such that $f$ and all its partial derivatives decay faster than any inverse power of $\|x\|$ as $\|x\| \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Admissible function
nodes.statement: $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{C}$ is admissible if there exists $\delta > 0$ with $|f(x)|$ and $|\widehat{f}(x)|$ bounded above by a constant times $(1+|x|)^{-d-\delta}$.

nodes.name: Optimal function
nodes.statement: An admissible function $f: \mathbb{R}^8 \to \mathbb{R}$ is optimal if it satisfies the Cohn-Elkies conditions (\ref{eqn: Cohn-Elkies condition 1})-(\ref{eqn: Cohn-Elkies condition 2}) and $f(0)/\widehat{f}(0) = 2^4$.

nodes.name: Modular group and congruence subgroups
nodes.statement: $\Gamma(1) := \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ acts on the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ by linear fractional transformations; $\Gamma(N)$ is the level $N$ principal congruence subgroup, and $\Gamma_0(N) = \{\binom{a\,b}{c\,d} \in \Gamma(1) \mid c \equiv 0 \pmod{N}\}$.

nodes.name: Slash operator and automorphy factor
nodes.statement: $j_k(z,\gamma) := (cz+d)^{-k}$ is the weight-$k$ automorphy factor; $(F|_k\gamma)(z) := j_k(z,\gamma)\, F(\gamma z)$ is the slash operator.

nodes.name: Holomorphic modular form
nodes.statement: A holomorphic $f: \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that (i) $f|_k\gamma = f$ for all $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and (ii) for each $\alpha \in \Gamma(1)$, $f|_k\alpha$ has a Fourier expansion $\sum_{n \geq 0} c_f(\alpha, n/n_\alpha)\, e^{2\pi i (n/n_\alpha) z}$.

nodes.name: Eisenstein series $E_k$
nodes.statement: For even $k \geq 4$, $E_k(z) := \frac{1}{2\zeta(k)} \sum_{(c,d) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \setminus (0,0)} (cz+d)^{-k}$, with Fourier expansion $E_k(z) = 1 + \frac{2}{\zeta(1-k)} \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sigma_{k-1}(n)\, e^{2\pi i n z}$.

nodes.name: Quasimodular form $E_2$
nodes.statement: $E_2(z) := 1 - 24 \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sigma_1(n)\, e^{2\pi i n z}$; not modular, but satisfies $z^{-2} E_2(-1/z) = E_2(z) - \frac{6i}{\pi z}$.

nodes.name: Theta functions (Thetanullwerte)
nodes.statement: $\theta_{00}(z) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} e^{\pi i n^2 z}$, $\theta_{01}(z) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} (-1)^n e^{\pi i n^2 z}$, $\theta_{10}(z) = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} e^{\pi i (n+1/2)^2 z}$; the fourth powers belong to $M_2(\Gamma(2))$.

nodes.name: Weakly-holomorphic modular form
nodes.statement: Holomorphic $f: \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ with $f|_k\gamma = f$ for $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and Fourier expansion $f|_k\alpha(z) = \sum_{n \geq n_0} c_f(\alpha, n/n_\alpha) e^{2\pi i (n/n_\alpha) z}$ for some $n_0 \in \mathbb{Z}$. The space is denoted $M_k^!(\Gamma)$.

nodes.name: Elliptic $j$-invariant
nodes.statement: $j := \frac{1728\, E_4^3}{E_4^3 - E_6^2} \in M_0^!(\Gamma(1))$, with Fourier expansion $j(z) = q^{-1} + 744 + 196884 q + \cdots$ where $q = e^{2\pi i z}$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary modular forms $\varphi_{-2}, \varphi_{-4}$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points

nodes.name: Auxiliary functions $\phi_{-4}, \phi_{-2}, \phi_0$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points

nodes.name: Function $a$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points

nodes.name: Modular form $h$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points

nodes.name: Auxiliary functions $\psi_I, \psi_T, \psi_S$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points

nodes.name: Function $b$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: $b(x) := \int_{-1}^{i} \psi_T(z) e^{\pi i \|x\|^2 z} dz + \int_{1}^{i} \psi_T(z) e^{\pi i \|x\|^2 z} dz - 2\int_{0}^{i} \psi_I(z) e^{\pi i \|x\|^2 z} dz - 2\int_{i}^{i\infty} \psi_S(z) e^{\pi i \|x\|^2 z} dz$.

nodes.name: Main theorem (sphere packing in dimension 8)
nodes.statement: No packing of unit balls in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^8$ has density greater than that of the $E_8$-lattice packing; equivalently $\Delta_8 = \pi^4/384$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^8$ is a sphere packing of unit balls

nodes.name: Cohn-Elkies linear programming bound
nodes.statement: Suppose $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is admissible, not identically zero, $f(x) \leq 0$ for $\|x\| \geq 1$, and $\widehat{f}(x) \geq 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$. Then the density of $d$-dimensional sphere packings is bounded above by $\frac{f(0)}{\widehat{f}(0)} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}\, B_d(0, 1/2)$.
assumptions: $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is admissible and not identically zero

nodes.name: Existence of magic Schwartz function $g$
nodes.statement: There exists a radial Schwartz function $g: \mathbb{R}^8 \to \mathbb{R}$ with $g(x) \leq 0$ for $\|x\| \geq \sqrt{2}$, $\widehat{g}(x) \geq 0$ for all $x$, and $g(0) = \widehat{g}(0) = 1$. Moreover $g(x), \widehat{g}(x)$ do not vanish for $\|x\|^2 \notin 2\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.

nodes.name: Construction of magic function $g = \frac{\pi i}{8640} a + \frac{i}{240\pi} b$
nodes.statement: The function $g(x) := \frac{\pi i}{8640} a(x) + \frac{i}{240\pi} b(x)$ satisfies the conditions of Theorem 3 (sign conditions on $g$ and $\widehat{g}$, and $g(0) = \widehat{g}(0) = 1$).
assumptions: $a, b: \mathbb{R}^8 \to i\mathbb{R}$ are the radial Schwartz functions of Section 4

nodes.name: Function $a$ is a Fourier eigenfunction (eigenvalue $+1$)
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: The function $a$ defined by the contour-integral formula belongs to the Schwartz space and satisfies $\widehat{a}(x) = a(x)$.
assumptions: $a$ defined by the contour-integral formula in eq. (a(r) definition)

nodes.name: Function $a$ has double zeroes at $\Lambda_8$-points of length $> \sqrt{2}$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: For $r > \sqrt{2}$, $a(r) = -4 \sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_{0}^{i\infty} \phi_0(-1/z) z^2 e^{\pi i r^2 z} dz$.
conclusions: $a(r) = -4\sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^{i\infty} \phi_0(-1/z) z^2 e^{\pi i r^2 z} dz$

nodes.name: Alternative integral representation of $a$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
conclusions: closed-form integral representation of $a(r)$ valid on $[0,\infty)$

nodes.name: Special values of $a$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points

nodes.name: Function $b$ is a Fourier eigenfunction (eigenvalue $-1$)
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: The function $b$ defined by its contour-integral formula belongs to the Schwartz space and satisfies $\widehat{b}(x) = -b(x)$.
assumptions: $b$ defined by the contour-integral formula in eq. (b(r) definition)

nodes.name: Function $b$ has double zeroes at $\Lambda_8$-points of length $> \sqrt{2}$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: For $r > \sqrt{2}$, $b(r) = -4 \sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_{0}^{i\infty} \psi_I(z) e^{\pi i r^2 z} dz$.
conclusions: $b(r) = -4 \sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^{i\infty} \psi_I(z) e^{\pi i r^2 z} dz$

nodes.name: Alternative integral representation of $b$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: For $r \geq 0$, $b(r) = 4i \sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \Big( \frac{144}{\pi r^2} + \frac{1}{\pi(r^2-2)} + \int_0^\infty (\psi_I(it) - 144 - e^{2\pi t}) e^{-\pi r^2 t} dt \Big)$.
conclusions: closed-form integral representation of $b(r)$ valid on $[0,\infty)$

nodes.name: Special values of $b$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points

nodes.name: Poisson summation for $E_8$
nodes.statement: $\sum_{\ell \in \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Lambda_8} f(\ell) = 2^4 \sum_{\ell \in \sqrt{2} \Lambda_8} \widehat{f}(\ell)$, the Poisson summation formula applied to $\Lambda_8$.

nodes.name: $\phi_0$ transformation rule
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points

nodes.name: $\psi$ identity $\psi_T + \psi_S = \psi_I$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: $\psi_T + \psi_S = \psi_I$.

nodes.name: Fourier transform of Gaussian
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}(e^{\pi i \|x\|^2 z})(y) = z^{-4} e^{\pi i \|y\|^2 (-1/z)}$ (in dimension 8).

nodes.name: Proof that $\widehat{a} = a$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: Estimate $a$ as Schwartz via $K_1$-Bessel bounds; then exchange contour integral and Fourier transform via Gaussian formula; substitute $w = -1/z$ and use $1$-periodicity of $\phi_0$ to recover $a(y)$.

nodes.name: Proof of double zeroes of $a$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: Denote the right-hand side by $d(r)$; deform the contours; apply the $\phi_0$ transformation rule to express the combination $\phi_0(-1/(z+1))(z+1)^2 - 2\phi_0(-1/z) z^2 + \phi_0(-1/(z-1))(z-1)^2 = 2\phi_0(z)$; conclude $d(r) = a(r)$.

nodes.name: Proof of alternative integral representation of $a$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: For $r > \sqrt{2}$ apply Proposition prop: a(r) double zeroes; subtract the asymptotic part of $\phi_0(i/t) t^2$ as $t \to \infty$; then extend by analyticity to $[0,\infty)$.

nodes.name: Proof of special values of $a$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: Direct evaluation of the alternative integral representation at $r = 0$ and $r = \sqrt{2}$.

nodes.name: Proof that $\widehat{b} = -b$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: Bound $b$ as Schwartz via $K_1$-Bessel estimates; exchange contour and Fourier integration; change variables $w = -1/z$; apply $\psi_T|_{-2} S = -\psi_T$, $\psi_I|_{-2} S = \psi_S$, $\psi_S|_{-2} S = \psi_I$ to obtain $\mathcal{F}(b)(x) = -b(x)$.

nodes.name: Proof of double zeroes of $b$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: Define $c(r)$ as right-hand side; rewrite as sum of three contour integrals; deform contours to height $i$; verify identity $\psi_T + \psi_S = \psi_I$ via group-theoretic manipulations in $\Gamma_0(2)$; conclude $c(r) = b(r)$.

nodes.name: Proof of alternative integral representation of $b$
nodes.section: 4 Fourier eigenfunctions with double zeroes at lattice points
nodes.statement: Analogous to the proof for $a$: use the double-zeros formula for $r > \sqrt{2}$; subtract the asymptotic part of $\psi_I(it)$ as $t \to \infty$; extend by analyticity to $[0,\infty)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem g (sign and normalization conditions on $g$)
nodes.statement: Show $g(r) \leq 0$ for $r \geq \sqrt{2}$ via $A(t) < 0$; show $\widehat{g}(r) \geq 0$ for $r > 0$ via $B(t) > 0$; verify $g(0) = \widehat{g}(0) = 1$ from the special values of $a$ and $b$.

nodes.name: Proof of main theorem (sphere packing in dimension 8)
nodes.statement: Apply Cohn-Elkies (Theorem 2) to the optimal function $f(x) = g(\sqrt{2} x)$; the optimality $f(0)/\widehat{f}(0) = 2^4$ then gives $\Delta_8 \leq 2^4 \cdot \mathrm{Vol}\, B_8(0,1/2) = \pi^4/384$, matched by the $E_8$ packing.

nodes.name: $E_8$ uniqueness as densest periodic packing
nodes.statement: The function $g$ satisfies the conclusions of Cohn-Elkies Conjecture 8.1, implying the $E_8$-lattice sphere packing is the unique periodic packing of maximal density in $\mathbb{R}^8$.

nodes.name: Forced double zeroes from Poisson summation
nodes.statement: Conditions (\ref{eqn: g1})-(\ref{eqn: g3}) combined with the Poisson summation formula on $\Lambda_8$ force $g(\ell) = \widehat{g}(\ell) = 0$ and the radial derivatives to vanish at all $\ell \in \Lambda_8 \setminus \{0\}$ of length $> \sqrt{2}$, motivating the integral-transform construction.

nodes.name: Sphere packing problem in dimension 8
nodes.statement: Determine the sphere packing constant $\Delta_8 := \sup_{\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^8 \text{ packing}} \Delta_{\mathcal{P}}$.

nodes.name: Estimate first contour-integral summand via Bessel $K_1$
nodes.statement: Use $|\phi_0(z)| \leq C e^{-2\pi \Im z}$ for $\Im z > 1/2$ to bound $\big|\int_{-1}^{i} \phi_0(-1/(z+1))(z+1)^2 e^{\pi i r^2 z} dz\big| \leq C_2 r K_1(2\sqrt{2}\pi r)$, with analogous bounds for the other three summands; conclude $a$ is Schwartz.

nodes.name: Exchange contour integral with Fourier transform
nodes.statement: Since the double integral converges absolutely, swap order and apply the Gaussian Fourier transform $\mathcal{F}(e^{\pi i \|x\|^2 z})(y) = z^{-4} e^{\pi i \|y\|^2 (-1/z)}$ inside each of the four integrals.

nodes.name: Substitute $w = -1/z$ and use $1$-periodicity of $\phi_0$
nodes.statement: After the change of variables and applying $1$-periodicity of $\phi_0$, the four integrals reassemble into the original definition of $a(y)$, giving $\widehat{a}(y) = a(y)$.

nodes.name: Set up auxiliary function $d(r)$
nodes.statement: Denote $d(r) := -4\sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^{i\infty} \phi_0(-1/z) z^2 e^{\pi i r^2 z} dz$ and verify convergence for $r > \sqrt{2}$ from the asymptotics of $\phi_0(-1/(it))$ as $t \to 0$ and $t \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Deform contours to height $i$
nodes.statement: For $r > \sqrt{2}$, $\phi_0(-1/z) z^2 e^{\pi i r^2 z} \to 0$ as $\Im z \to \infty$, so deform each contour through $z = i$ and split into pieces from $-1, 0, 1$ to $i$ and from $i$ to $i\infty$.

nodes.name: Apply $\phi_0$ transformation rule
nodes.statement: Use eq. (phi0 transform) to verify $\phi_0(-1/(z+1))(z+1)^2 - 2\phi_0(-1/z) z^2 + \phi_0(-1/(z-1))(z-1)^2 = 2\phi_0(z)$ (the $\phi_{-2}$ and $\phi_{-4}$ contributions cancel since both are $1$-periodic and the operator is a discrete second difference).

nodes.name: Conclude $d(r) = a(r)$
nodes.statement: Substituting the identity from step 3 into the deformed integrals collapses $d(r)$ to the definition of $a(r)$.

nodes.name: Bessel $K_1$ estimate for $b$ summands
nodes.statement: Using $|\psi_S(z)| \leq C e^{-\pi \Im z}$ for $\Im z > 1/2$ and an $S$-substitution to convert $\psi_T$-integrals to $\psi_S$-integrals, obtain $|b(r)| \leq C_2 r K_1(2\pi r) + C_3 e^{-\pi(r^2+1)}/(r^2+1)$, hence $b$ is Schwartz.

nodes.name: Exchange contour integration and Fourier transform
nodes.statement: Apply the Gaussian Fourier identity inside each of the four integrals defining $b$, then change variables $w = -1/z$.

nodes.name: Apply slash-operator identities $\psi_T|_{-2}S = -\psi_T$, $\psi_I|_{-2}S = \psi_S$, $\psi_S|_{-2}S = \psi_I$
nodes.statement: These three identities, immediate from the definitions \eqref{eqn: psi I define}-\eqref{eqn: psi S define}, transform the four integrals so they match the definition of $b$ with overall sign $-1$, giving $\mathcal{F}(b)(x) = -b(x)$.

nodes.name: Set up $c(r)$ and contour split
nodes.statement: Let $c(r) := -4\sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^{i\infty} \psi_I(z) e^{\pi i r^2 z} dz$; rewrite as a sum of three integrals with contours starting at $-1, 0, 1$ shifted to $i\infty$; deform to height $i$.

nodes.name: Prove identity $\psi_T + \psi_S = \psi_I$
nodes.statement: From the definitions $\psi_T + \psi_S = h|_{-2}T - h|_{-2}ST^2 + h|_{-2}S - h|_{-2}STS$; using $ST^2S, T, STS(ST)^{-1} \in \Gamma_0(2)$ and $h \in M^!_{-2}(\Gamma_0(2))$, this collapses to $h - h|_{-2}ST = \psi_I$.

nodes.name: Combine to conclude $c(r) = b(r)$
nodes.statement: Substitute $\psi_T + \psi_S = \psi_I$ into the contour-deformed expression for $c(r)$ to recover the definition of $b(r)$.

nodes.name: Reduce $g(r) \leq 0$ on $[\sqrt{2}, \infty)$ to negativity of $A(t)$
nodes.statement: By the double-zeros propositions for $a$ and $b$, for $r > \sqrt{2}$ one has $g(r) = \frac{\pi}{2160} \sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^\infty A(t) e^{-\pi r^2 t} dt$ where $A(t) = -t^2 \phi_0(i/t) - \frac{36}{\pi^2} \psi_I(it)$. It thus suffices to show $A(t) < 0$ on $(0, \infty)$.

nodes.name: Compute asymptotic expansions $A_0^{(6)}$ and $A_\infty^{(6)}$
nodes.statement: Using the Fourier expansions (phi fourier4)-(phi fourier0), (psi fourier I), (psi fourier S) and the transformation rule (phi0 transform), compute closed forms for $A_0^{(6)}(t)$ (asymptotic at $0$) and $A_\infty^{(6)}(t)$ (asymptotic at $\infty$), each accurate up to $O(t^2 e^{-6\pi/t})$ resp. $O(t^2 e^{-6\pi t})$.

nodes.name: Bound Fourier-coefficient errors via Bruinier estimate
nodes.statement: By the convergent asymptotic expansion for Fourier coefficients of weakly-holomorphic modular forms (Bruinier, Prop. 1.12), $|c_{\psi_I}(n)| \leq e^{4\pi\sqrt{n}}$ and similar bounds for $\psi_S, \phi_0, \phi_{-2}, \phi_{-4}$, giving explicit bounds $R_0^{(6)}$ and $R_\infty^{(6)}$ on the truncation error of $A$.

nodes.name: Interval-arithmetic verification on $(0,1]$ and $[1,\infty)$
nodes.statement: Interval-arithmetic computation verifies $|R_0^{(6)}(t)| \leq |A_0^{(6)}(t)|$ and $A_0^{(6)}(t) < 0$ on $(0,1]$, and $|R_\infty^{(6)}(t)| \leq |A_\infty^{(6)}(t)|$ and $A_\infty^{(6)}(t) < 0$ on $[1,\infty)$, hence $A(t) < 0$ on $(0,\infty)$, proving (g1).

nodes.name: Reduce $\widehat{g}(r) \geq 0$ to positivity of $B(t)$
nodes.statement: From the alternative integral representations of $a$ and $b$, for $r > 0$ one has $\widehat{g}(r) = \frac{\pi}{2160} \sin(\pi r^2/2)^2 \int_0^\infty B(t) e^{-\pi r^2 t} dt$ where $B(t) = -t^2 \phi_0(i/t) + \frac{36}{\pi^2} \psi_I(it)$. It suffices to show $B(t) > 0$ on $(0,\infty)$.

nodes.name: Interval-arithmetic verification of $B(t) > 0$
nodes.statement: Compute $B_0^{(6)}, B_\infty^{(6)}$; using the same Fourier-coefficient bounds, verify $|R_0^{(6)}| \leq |B_0^{(6)}|$ and $B_0^{(6)} > 0$ on $(0,1]$, and analogously on $[1,\infty)$, proving (g2).

nodes.name: Verify normalization $g(0) = \widehat{g}(0) = 1$
nodes.statement: Property (g3) follows immediately from $a(0) = -i\, 8640/\pi$, $b(0) = 0$ (Propositions a values, b values), giving $g(0) = \frac{\pi i}{8640} \cdot \frac{-i\, 8640}{\pi} = 1$, and by the eigenfunction relations $\widehat{g}(0) = g(0) = 1$.

nodes.name: Set $f(x) := g(\sqrt{2} x)$ and apply Cohn-Elkies
nodes.statement: Define $f(x) := g(\sqrt{2} x)$. By Theorem 3, $f$ is admissible with $f(x) \leq 0$ for $\|x\| \geq 1$, $\widehat{f}(x) \geq 0$, and $f(0)/\widehat{f}(0) = 2^4$.

nodes.name: Read off the bound $\Delta_8 \leq \pi^4/384$
nodes.statement: Cohn-Elkies (Theorem 2) gives $\Delta_8 \leq 2^4 \cdot \mathrm{Vol}\, B_8(0,1/2) = 2^4 \cdot \frac{\pi^4}{2^8 \cdot 4!} = \pi^4/384$. Since the $E_8$-lattice packing achieves this density, $\Delta_8 = \pi^4/384$.
